payload.body:
You can make something work for a long time before you admit how much you have been adjusting yourself to keep it going. You adapt, make exceptions, tell yourself it is manageable, and then reach a point where changing the plan feels easier than having one more conversation about what is not working.

By the time you finally say no, the decision may feel obvious to you. Other people can be surprised because they did not hear all the smaller objections that came before it, or because you kept treating each problem like something you could manage.

The challenge is that independence can become easiest to claim at the point of departure. By then, you may already be so finished with the situation that you no longer know if it could have changed once your actual needs were on the table.

You are allowed to change your direction as you learn more about who you are. The question is if the situation had a chance to respond to the person you actually are before leaving became the only answer that felt honest.
